deliverables: Performance optimization including 2x to 10x improvements in snapshot signing and memory profile and reduced L1 fees through on-chain contract optimization.
Operational excellence including operator runbooks, simpler node configuration, observability and logging, and an improved TUI.
Ecosystem support including production-user and pipeline-integrator features, Hydra Alliance facilitation, hackathons, and developer relations.
Maintenance and developer experience including CI, tooling, and technical debt reduction.
request.what: Fund four Hydra v2 workstreams: performance optimization, operational excellence, ecosystem support, and developer experience/maintenance.

claims.claim: Hydra is described as the only production-grade Layer 2 on Cardano, already running live workloads for Delta DeFi, Masumi, Intersect, VTech Labs, Blockfrost, Midgard, and others.
The proposal requests ₳5,100,781 and says funding will be milestone-gated with independent third-party assurance and Intersect administrative treasury governance.
Hydra lets participants transact with sub-second finality, near-zero or zero internal fees, high throughput, and Cardano L1 settlement as the security backstop.
The proposer claims Cardano L1 has over two hours of finality, about $0.17 per transaction, and roughly 7 to 10 TPS, while competing platforms offer materially faster and cheaper performance.
The funded performance workstream is expected to deliver 2x to 10x improvements in snapshot signing and memory profile and reduce L1 fees through on-chain contract optimization.

The proposer claims Hydra can increase Cardano TVL, active users, transactions, throughput, reliability, protocol revenue, and adoption by enabling high-performance applications that are impractical on L1.
The proposer says Hydra activity can create L1 fee accrual through head opening, fund changes, closure, and optional routing of internal head fees to the L1 treasury on settlement.

The proposal identifies current and future use cases including institutional DEXes, agent-to-agent commerce, B2B payments, prediction markets, RWA platforms, gaming, verifiable information processing, point of sale, and micropayments.
The proposer claims L1 upgrades such as Leios and Peras will help the base layer but cannot provide the zero-fee, sub-second, high-throughput envelope required by high-performance applications.

The document points to an external PDF proposal link in the abstract but the supplied anchor text itself does not include a budget breakdown, feasibility assessment, alternatives analysis, failure-mode analysis, or community impact analysis.

summary: The anchor requests ₳5,100,781 for Hydra v2 hardening and adoption workstreams, presenting Hydra as Cardano's production L2 for faster, cheaper, higher-throughput applications, but the supplied text relies heavily on proposer assertions and omits several diligence components identified by the deterministic assessment.
